next_state_election.name: Statewide General Election
next_state_election.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — General Election Calendars

glance_notes.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — 2026 General Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadlines: South Carolina's registration deadline varies by method for the November 3, 2026 General Election. In-person registration is due by 5:00 p.m. October 2, online, fax or email registration is due by 11:59 p.m. October 4, and mailed applications must be postmarked by October 5.

glance_notes.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Early Voting
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 19–31: All registered South Carolina voters may vote early without an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting runs October 19 through October 31, Monday through Saturday, with centers closed Sunday, October 25.

glance_notes.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Photo ID Requirements
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required In Person: South Carolina generally requires one of the state's accepted current and valid photo IDs when voting in person. Voters who cannot obtain a qualifying photo ID because of a reasonable impediment have a provisional-ballot option using their non-photo voter registration card and an affidavit.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible South Carolina residents may register online, by mail, by fax, by email or in person through a county voter registration and elections office. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on or before the next election, reside in South Carolina in the county and precinct where registering, not be under a court order declaring the person mentally incompetent, and meet South Carolina's rules concerning criminal convictions. A person convicted of a felony or an offense against election laws may register after serving the entire sentence, including probation or parole, or after receiving a pardon. South Carolina does not impose a minimum length-of-residency requirement before a person may register, but registration must be completed in time for the applicable election deadline.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, fax, email or in-person registration
register.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: South Carolina requires completion of the entire sentence, including probation or parole, following a felony or election-law conviction unless the person has received a pardon. This differs from states that restore voting rights immediately upon release from incarceration. The State Election Commission explicitly states there is no length-of-residency requirement for registration.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use South Carolina's MySCVotes system to check your voter registration, update voter information, obtain a sample ballot, find your polling place, view voting history and check absentee or provisional-ballot status. Voters who find incorrect information should contact their county voter registration and elections office.
check_registration.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Voters
check_registration.internal_note: The State Election Commission identifies MySCVotes as the central voter portal for registration lookup and updates, sample ballots, polling places, voting history, absentee status, provisional-ballot status and county-office information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: South Carolina generally requires registration at least 30 days before an election, but the exact 2026 General Election deadline varies by registration method because the 30th day falls on a weekend. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person registration is due by 5:00 p.m. Friday, October 2 unless the county office holds weekend hours. Online registration and applications submitted by fax or email are due by 11:59 p.m. Sunday, October 4. Registration applications submitted by mail must be postmarked by Monday, October 5. South Carolina does not provide general same-day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — 2026 General Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: Do not reduce South Carolina's 2026 registration deadline to a single date. The official calendar establishes three operative deadlines: October 2 at 5:00 p.m. for ordinary in-person registration, October 4 at 11:59 p.m. for online/fax/email registration, and an October 5 postmark deadline for mail. A county office that holds weekend hours may affect the practical in-person deadline.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use MySCVotes to find the Election Day polling place assigned to your registered address. Election Day voters should vote at their assigned polling place. Early voting uses separate early-voting centers, and a registered voter may use any early-voting center located within the voter's county during the statewide early-voting period. Polling places can change, so voters should confirm their assigned location before Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place through MySCVotes
polling_place.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — MySCVotes
polling_place.internal_note: The State Election Commission directs voters to MySCVotes for Election Day polling-place information. Early voting is different: voters may visit any early-voting center within their county. Reverify Election Day locations close to November 3.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: South Carolina's Statewide General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is in line at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote. Voters should go to their assigned polling place and generally must present one of South Carolina's accepted current and valid photo IDs. A voter who does not have qualifying photo identification may still have a provisional-ballot option under the state's reasonable-impediment or ID-cure procedures.
election_day.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — 2026 General Election Calendar
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election calendar confirms 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. statewide polling hours. State voter information confirms voters in line at 7:00 p.m. may vote. The photo-ID rule includes both a reasonable-impediment exception and a provisional cure procedure when a voter simply lacks the ID at the polls.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: South Carolina polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone who is in line at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — 2026 General Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar and current voter information confirm uniform statewide General Election polling hours of 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: All registered South Carolina voters may vote early in person without an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 Statewide General Election, early voting begins Monday, October 19 and ends Saturday, October 31. Early-voting centers are open Monday through Saturday and closed Sunday, October 25. The official 2026 General Election calendar lists hours of 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. A voter may visit any early-voting center within the county where the voter is registered and must present qualifying photo identification under the same general ID rules used for Election Day voting.
early_voting.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — 2026 Statewide General Election Early Voting
early_voting.flagged_reason: The State Election Commission's current early-voting webpage contains an internal inconsistency: its 2026 General Election location section lists 8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m., while the official 2026 General Election calendar and candidate toolkit list 8:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. for October 19-31. The statutory general-election schedule and official calendar support 6:00 p.m.; this should be rechecked before publication.
early_voting.internal_note: IMPORTANT SOURCE CONFLICT FOUND DURING VERIFICATION. The current early-voting page says October 19-31 but displays 8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m. near the 2026 General Election section. The official 2026 General Election Calendar dated April 15, 2026 and the 2026 Candidate Filing Toolkit both state Monday-Saturday 8:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. and closed Sundays. The same early-voting webpage's general statutory description says statewide General Elections run Monday 15 days before Election Day through Saturday three days before Election Day. Use 6:00 p.m. based on the dedicated official 2026 calendar, but keep this section flagged until the SEC resolves or updates the conflicting webpage.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: South Carolina does not provide no-excuse absentee voting by mail. A registered voter must meet one of the state's qualifying reasons, such as being age 65 or older, having a physical disability, being absent from the county throughout the early-voting period and Election Day voting hours, or having qualifying employment, caregiving, confinement, military or emergency circumstances. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to apply for an absentee ballot is 5:00 p.m. October 23. A completed absentee ballot must be received by the county voter registration and elections office no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. The voter must sign the ballot oath and have the signature witnessed. A voter returning an absentee ballot in person must present photo identification.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Excuse required; apply by 5:00 p.m. October 23
absentee_mail.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: South Carolina differs from many states because ordinary absentee-by-mail voting remains excuse-based even though no-excuse early in-person voting is available. The official 2026 calendar establishes October 23 at 5:00 p.m. as the General Election absentee application deadline and November 3 at 7:00 p.m. as the ordinary ballot receipt deadline. Current SEC guidance confirms the witness requirement and photo-ID requirement for in-person absentee return. UOCAVA voters have separate rules.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: South Carolina generally requires voters to present one current and valid qualifying photo ID when voting in person. Accepted identification includes a South Carolina driver's license, a South Carolina DMV identification card, a South Carolina concealed weapons permit, a South Carolina voter registration card with photo, qualifying federal military identification or a U.S. passport or passport card. A voter who cannot obtain one of these IDs because of a reasonable impediment may present a current non-photo voter registration card, sign an affidavit explaining the impediment and cast a provisional ballot. A voter who simply forgot an acceptable photo ID may cast a provisional ballot and present qualifying photo ID to the county voter registration and elections office before certification for the ballot to count.
voter_id.glance_value: Current photo ID generally required; exceptions and provisional procedures available
voter_id.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Photo ID Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: The reasonable-impediment exception is significant and should not be omitted. Examples listed by the SEC include disability or illness, work conflict, lack of transportation, lack of a birth certificate, family responsibilities, religious objection to being photographed and any other obstacle the voter finds reasonable. Free photo voter-registration cards are available from county voter registration offices, and free identification cards are also available through the DMV.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: South Carolina provides accessible voting options and assistance for voters with disabilities. Polling places are expected to provide accessible parking, entrances and voting paths. South Carolina's ballot-marking devices are designed to allow voters with disabilities to vote independently. A voter with a disability, or a voter who is blind or unable to read or write, may receive assistance and generally may choose the person providing that assistance, except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer or an officer or agent of the voter's union. A voter who cannot access the polling place or stand in line because of a disability, or who is age 65 or older, may qualify for curbside voting from a vehicle. Voters with physical disabilities also qualify for absentee voting.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance, curbside and absentee options
accessible_voting.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The SEC directly confirms assistance rules, accessible polling-place features and curbside voting. Curbside voting does not require a disability parking placard. The voter must independently qualify for curbside voting; accompanying passengers do not automatically qualify. South Carolina's ExpressVote ballot-marking devices are designed for accessibility and produce a paper ballot.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: South Carolina provides special voting procedures for eligible members of the U.S. Armed Forces, Merchant Marine, qualifying government and service personnel overseas, eligible spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens residing outside the United States. Covered voters may submit a Federal Post Card Application to register and establish UOCAVA status and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when applicable. UOCAVA ballots are sent no later than 45 days before an election and may be delivered electronically. South Carolina also permits qualifying UOCAVA voters to return voted ballots electronically under its special procedures. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, ordinary UOCAVA ballots returned electronically must meet the applicable Election Day deadline, while qualifying mailed military and overseas ballots may be accepted through 5:00 p.m. November 5 under the state's 2026 election calendar.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery and special return procedures available
military_overseas.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Military & Overseas Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: The SEC's UOCAVA page confirms FPCA registration, 45-day ballot transmission and electronic ballot-return capability, including return by email under specified procedures. The official 2026 General Election Calendar states that ordinary absentee ballots are due at 7:00 p.m. November 3 while military and overseas voters' ballots are accepted through 5:00 p.m. November 5. UOCAVA-specific instructions should control because electronic and mailed return procedures differ.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students in South Carolina may register either where they reside while attending college, such as a dormitory, or at another South Carolina address they consider their voting residence and intend to return to, such as a family home. A student must choose only one voter registration address. Students registered at a college address may vote early at any early-voting center in that county or at their assigned Election Day polling place. Students who retain another South Carolina voting address may vote in that county and may qualify for absentee voting if they will be absent from the county throughout the early-voting period and Election Day voting hours. A college ID by itself is not an accepted form of identification for in-person voting under South Carolina's photo-ID law.
student_voting.glance_value: Choose one qualifying residence; college ID is not accepted for voting
student_voting.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — Students
student_voting.internal_note: The SEC student page explicitly states that a student may choose a college residence or another South Carolina residence but only one. It also explicitly states that a college ID cannot be used as the required ID to vote in person. A college ID may nevertheless help satisfy identification requirements during certain voter-registration methods, which should not be confused with the narrower Election Day photo-ID list.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Registered South Carolina voters can use MySCVotes to view their official sample ballot. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residence, districts and local contests, voters should use their own registration information to retrieve the ballot that applies to them. The sample ballot should be checked again close to the November 3, 2026 General Election after ballot preparation is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Get your sample ballot through MySCVotes
sample_ballot.source_name: South Carolina State Election Commission — MySCVotes
sample_ballot.internal_note: The State Election Commission lists Get My Sample Ballot as a core MySCVotes function. Ballots vary by residence and district. Reverify after final November ballots are published.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: South Carolina State Election Commission, 1122 Lady Street, Suite 500, Columbia, SC 29201. Phone: 803-734-9060. Email: elections@elections.sc.gov. For voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot, early-voting, polling-place or provisional-ballot questions, contact your county voter registration and elections office.
contact.internal_note: Current State Election Commission voter materials list 1122 Lady Street, Suite 500, Columbia, SC 29201 and 803-734-9060. The Commission's current voter education resources list [elections@elections.sc.gov](mailto:elections@elections.sc.gov). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the South Carolina State Election Commission and MySCVotes for official statewide election information. These resources provide voter registration, registration lookup and updates, polling places, sample ballots, early-voting locations, absentee-ballot information and tracking, provisional-ballot status, photo-ID requirements, military and overseas voting information and county election-office contacts. County voter registration and elections offices administer voter registration and many local election functions.
